subject: Kestrel onboarding: model shortlist, context sizing, token forecast
messages:

Subject: Kickoff + model/context questions for onboarding

Hi Karthik and Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — excited to move forward. We want to make the handoff to implementation this month. Before the kickoff, our ML team asked for a quick draft of model candidates plus estimates for context length needs and expected token volumes so we can align infra and data prep.

Quick background: our product is a semantic search + summarization assistant across internal docs. Typical doc length ranges from short (200 tokens) to long (up to 7,000 tokens). Expected queries per user are ~4/day during trial, projected 25k users in month 1 post-launch (we expect a phased ramp). We plan to use Redwood’s hosted API initially, then move to Dedicated if latencies hold.

Can you send a shortlist and a rough token forecast by EOD tomorrow? Also flag any obvious blockers for 7k-context support.

Appreciate it —
Elaine

Head of ML Ops, Kestrel AI
elaine@kestrel.ai
(650) 555-0192

Hi Elaine —

Thanks for the context and the token profile CSV — that's super helpful. I'll put together a concise model shortlist and a token-volume sketch and loop in Vanessa for the detailed workload sizing. Expect a 1-page shortlist + a traffic forecast by tomorrow EOD.

Immediate notes:
- 7k token docs are large but supported with model choices and chunking strategies; there will be trade-offs between latency and cost.
- We should decide asap whether you want single-step long-context generation (slower, higher cost) vs chunk+re-rank + summarization (faster, cheaper).

I'll follow up with Vanessa's recommended shortlist and concrete per-token throughput estimates.

Cheers,

Subject: Re: Kickoff + model/context questions for onboarding

Hi all — following Karthik's note, here's a concise model shortlist and a preliminary workload sizing. I attached a PDF with the same content and a short mutually agreed map (MAP) template.

Model shortlist (prioritized):
1) Open-Quant-7B (low-latency baseline)
   - Context support: 4k tokens native; with sliding-window we can support up to ~8k for extractive tasks but expect degraded single-step generation quality beyond 4k.
   - Latency: ~80–120 ms per token at 32-token step on Dedicated with 1:1 GPU mapping (approx).
   - Cost proxy: low; good for high QPS retrieval + short summarization flows.

2) LlamaX-13B (quality-focused mid-tier)
   - Context support: 8k tokens native; stable generation up to 8k.
   - Latency: ~120–220 ms per token depending on quantization; recommend 8-bit quant on Dedicated.
   - Cost proxy: moderate; strong quality on abstractive summarization.

3) Redwood-eden-30B (high quality, long-context)
   - Context support: 16k tokens native; best single-pass summarization for long docs.
   - Latency: ~250–400 ms per token at peak; higher cost but reduces multi-stage pipeline complexity.
   - Cost proxy: high; reserved for gold-tier summarization or high-fidelity answers.

Recommended pattern for Kestrel: start with a hybrid pipeline (Open-Quant-7B for retrieval/scoring + LlamaX-13B for final abstractive summary on medium docs). Reserve Redwood-eden-30B for >12k token docs or premium users.

Workload sizing (rough forecast, month 1 phased ramp):
- Trial users active: 25k (phased ramp over 4 weeks)
- Average queries/user/day: 4 -> 100k queries/day at full ramp
- Token per query (avg): retrieval + prompt overhead ~400 tokens; summarization output ~200 tokens => approx 600 tokens/query average for hybrid flow.
- Total tokens/day (hybrid): 100k * 600 = 60M tokens/day.
- Peak concurrent QPS estimate: 15–25 QPS (depends on geography, peak hours) — recommend capacity for 40 QPS headroom during initial launch.

Notes on 7k+ documents:
- If you need single-pass summarization for full 7k contexts, LlamaX-13B (8k) will be at the upper bound; Redwood-eden-30B gives safer headroom but cost increases materially.
- Chunk+re-rank approach: chunk documents into ~1.5–2k segments, run retrieval & per-chunk scoring on Open-Quant-7B, then aggregate and run final summarization on LlamaX-13B. This reduces cost by ~40–60% vs single-pass 8k+ generation and gives competitive latency.

Attachments: model_shortlist_and_notes.pdf (shortlist + decision matrix), Kestrel_Redwood_MAP_v1.xlsx (mutual action plan template)

I'll be at the kickoff; Monica will lead the implementation sprints once we sign the MAP and confirm model tiering. Happy to walk through any of the numbers live.

- Vanessa Ortiz
Solution Architect, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai

From: Elaine Park <elaine@kestrel.ai>

Vanessa — thanks, this is exactly what we needed. A couple quick clarifications:

1) When you say 600 tokens/query average for the hybrid flow, does that include embedding calls for retrieval or only generation tokens? Our pipeline uses embeddings for index retrieval (about 128 tokens/input) — should that be added on top?

2) For chunk+re-rank, can you confirm an example end-to-end latency estimate for a 7k doc (chunk into 2k pieces) for the hybrid pipeline (Open-Quant chunk scoring + LlamaX final summary) — ballpark tail latency for user-facing summary?

We'd like these clarified so our infra and cost models match. If helpful, we can share a sample doc to test.

Thanks —
Elaine

Hi Elaine & team —

Quick answers and next steps from the implementation side:

1) Embeddings: Vanessa's 600 tokens/query was generation-focused and included prompt overhead but not embeddings. Add embedding tokens (~128 per retrieval call) on top for the retrieval step. For planning let's use 600 + 128 = ~728 tokens/query.

2) Latency for chunk+re-rank (example 7k doc -> 4 chunks @ ~1.75k tokens):
   - Open-Quant chunk scoring (per chunk): ~40–60 ms per token peak for short steps; scoring parallelized across chunks -> effective per-chunk time ~300–700 ms depending on concurrency.
   - Re-rank + assemble: ~150–300 ms.
   - Final summarization on LlamaX-13B (single pass on aggregated context): ~1.5–3.5 s tail latency depending on quantization and batch/pinning choices.
   - End-to-end user-facing tail latency (95th): ~2–5 seconds for the chunk+re-rank + LlamaX flow with Recommended Dedicated sizing (1:1 GPU mapping for scoring + a small pool for summarization).

3) Capacity ask: Based on the adjusted token estimate (728 tokens/query), full-ramp tokens/day = 100k * 728 = 72.8M tokens/day. Recommend initial reserved capacity to handle 40 QPS sustained with autoscale up to 120 QPS for bursts. We'll include a breakdown in the MAP and sizing sheet.

Next steps:
- I'll attach a short ops checklist for Dedicated vs Hosted run (network egress, KMS, auditing).
- Karthik will schedule the kickoff for next Tue; please confirm that date/time works for the Kestrel ML team.

If you want, send a sample doc and we can run a quick proof-of-concept within our sandbox to measure real latency.

Cheers,
Monica Patel
Implementation Lead, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.ai
